text:
Mason McTavish's move to St. Louis has handed him a bigger job. He's on the ice for 63% of the Blues' power-play chances, up from 36% last season, and his own chances have jumped to 1.74 expected goals per 60 minutes from 1.22. Seven goals in 17 games is the result, and our breakout flag is on, with the usual warning that 17 games is a small sample.

The Hockey News noticed the other side this week, writing that he has "Gone Cold" since a hot start to his Blues career, and the last ten games bear that out: four points where our numbers expected closer to seven. That stretch looks like noise rather than decline, because the chances are still there and he's scoring about a goal below what they deserve. The real question is defense. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more with him on the ice last season than against almost any forward. Saturday's 12 and a half minutes against Nashville, his lowest in ten games, is worth watching. If the minutes hold, the goals should follow.
headline: A bigger job in St. Louis
